about: Tonbo is a Bengaluru-based global defence electronics OEM that designs sensing, processing, communication and guidance systems such as thermal weapon sights, thermal binoculars, targeting and fire-control systems and missile seekers. It owns its IP and outsources manufacturing to EMS partners (asset-light). Over 28,000 systems have been deployed across 24 countries as of June 30, 2026.

peers.name: Paras Defence and Space Technologies Limited

objects.purpose: Offer for Sale by Selling Shareholders (no proceeds to the Company; listing benefits only)

promoters.background: Founder-technologists with over 21 years of working together; previously with the US Department of Defense and Sarnoff Corporation. Promoters' shares are not pledged.

concentration.note: FY26: top 5 customers 53.03% and top 10 77.83% of revenue; largest customer 13.78% (was 57.07% in FY25, 44.11% in FY24). Indian Government 71.19% of FY26 revenue (foreign government a further 3.34%).

litigation_note: Company, MD Arvind Kondangi Lakshmikumar and a nominee director are named in a suit filed in the Singapore High Court by a minority shareholder of CEAQ Singapore. Anonymous complaints were made to SEBI, the Ministry of Defence and others after the earlier DRHP. Bank guarantees of Rs 78.93 crore are listed under contingent liabilities.
strengths: Largest manufacturer of thermal imaging systems for Indian government and defence agencies (Apr 2024 to Mar 2026) and 94% share of India's thermal imaging exports by units, per the F&S report.
Owns 100% of its intellectual property since Fiscal 2024, so it has no dependence on external technology partners.
ITAR-free EO/IR products let it sell to export-sensitive markets; over 28,000 systems deployed across 24 countries.
Asset-light model with outsourced manufacturing to EMS partners such as Kaynes keeps capital spending low.
Confirmed order book of Rs 314.24 crore at June 30, 2026, plus Rs 118.15 crore of new orders received from July to September 2026.
In-house R&D team of 130 engineers (about 38% of staff), with R&D spend rising to Rs 25.86 crore in FY26 from Rs 4.24 crore in FY24.
Healthy EBITDA margins of 26% to 30% across FY24 to FY26 and a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.21 in FY26.
Platform systems (integrated autonomous solutions) grew from Rs 12.70 crore in FY24 to Rs 144.81 crore in FY26.

risks.title: Revenue fell and Q1FY27 swung to a loss
risks.detail: Revenue fell 22.69% to Rs 362.65 crore in FY26 and PAT fell to Rs 50.88 crore from Rs 72.76 crore. The June 2026 quarter showed a loss of Rs 17.74 crore on revenue of Rs 36.01 crore, as orders are lumpy and back-ended.

risks.title: Negative operating cash flow and stretched working capital
risks.detail: Operating cash flow was negative Rs 136.12 crore in FY25 and negative Rs 63.22 crore in FY26. Working capital days rose from 152 in FY24 to 280 in FY25 and 517 in FY26.

risks.title: Government and tender dependence with poor revenue visibility
risks.detail: Business is cyclical, tied to government budgets and short, non-recurring tender contracts. Indian Government was 71.19% of FY26 revenue and revenue was 57.07% from a single customer in FY25.

risks.title: Customer concentration
risks.detail: Top 5 customers made up 53.03% and top 10 made up 77.83% of FY26 revenue. In FY25 the top 10 were 95.49% of revenue.

risks.title: Heavy dependence on limited suppliers and contract manufacturers
risks.detail: Critical components (IR focal plane arrays, OLED micro displays) come from a narrow global supplier base. Top ten suppliers were 68.77% of total expenses in FY26. Large-scale manufacturing is fully outsourced.

risks.title: Export revenue is volatile
risks.detail: Exports were 48.61% of revenue in FY24 and 65.52% in FY25 but only 5.57% in FY26 and 0.25% in the June 2026 quarter, making geographic exposure swing sharply.

risks.title: Product concentration in tactical systems
risks.detail: Tactical systems were 83.90% of revenue in FY24, 77.24% in FY25 and 58.37% in FY26, so demand for these sights remains a key driver.

risks.title: Pending legal matters and regulatory filing delays
risks.detail: A Singapore High Court suit names the company, its MD and a nominee director. Anonymous complaints were filed with SEBI and the Ministry of Defence. There were also delays in RoC filings in FY24, FY25 and FY26.

notes: RHP: price band, issue size in Rs, P/E and Offer size are blank (null). Offer is 100% Offer for Sale of up to 12,174,046 shares, no fresh issue, no proceeds to the Company. FY24 is STANDALONE (no subsidiaries before FY25); FY25 and FY26 are consolidated. Source figures are in Rs million, converted to Rs crore. The June 2026 quarter stub is ignored in arrays (revenue Rs 36.01 crore, PAT -Rs 17.74 crore, EPS -3.20). PAT margin is the reported PAT / total income. Net worth, borrowings and cash match the RHP; cash_and_bank is cash plus other bank balances (excluding term deposits). debt_equity and current_ratio are computed from borrowings / net worth and current assets / current liabilities because they are not reported. FY24 basic EPS 62.61 versus diluted 13.63 is as reported. Operating cash flow derived as net cash change minus investing and financing, matching the RHP risk factor for FY25 and FY26. Promoter post-offer holding 14.01% is computed: 9,982,600 minus 1,960,000 promoter shares offered, over 57,282,100.
